page_title: Autonomous LLM-driven research from data to human-verifiable research papers

sources.entry: data-to-paper* is a framework for systematically navigating the power of AI to perform complete end-to-end

summary.name: data-to-paper
summary.one_liner: An arXiv research paper describing data-to-paper, an automation platform where interacting LLM agents carry out a stepwise research process from annotated data to a traceable, human-verifiable manuscript.
use_cases: generating research papers from annotated datasets
summary.what_it_does: The paper describes data-to-paper, a platform that guides interacting LLM agents through a complete stepwise research process. In autopilot mode, given only annotated data, it raises hypotheses, designs research plans, writes and debugs analysis code, generates and interprets results, and produces a research manuscript. It programmatically back-traces information flow so results, methods and data can be chained together. Human oversight and interaction are supported. The authors report that for simple goals, fully autonomous cycles produced manuscripts recapitulating peer-reviewed publications without major errors in about 80-90% of cases, while more complex goals required human co-piloting. Novelty of the generated research was described as relatively limited.
notable: Programmatic back-tracing of information flow so every result links to its methods and data
Autopilot mode runs hypothesis, planning, coding, and writing without human input
Human co-piloting supported and reported as critical for complex goals
Reported 80-90% recapitulation without major errors on simple research goals
caveats: Novelty of generated research was relatively limited according to the authors
Accuracy drops as goal complexity increases, requiring human co-piloting
Platform availability, licensing and pricing are not stated on the page
